messages.subject: sumstats function for  meta-analysis
parts:
Hi,

I am working with summary statistics derived from METAL's fixed effect  meta-analysis (Effect Size and Standard Error Based Analysis). All the traits are binary. My question is in the sumstats function, should I specify OLS=FALSE and se.logit =TRUE for all the traits?
  
Thank you very much for your help!
Lu

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: sumstats function for meta-analysis
parts:
Hi Lu, 

If the standard error column is the standard error of the odds ratio you would set se.logit = FALSE, and if it is the standard error of a logsitic beta you would set se.logit = TRUE. Off the top of my head I'm not positive for METAL output what the scale of the standard error column is, but my guess is that it is the standard error of a logistic beta in which case as you say you would set se.logit = TRUE (but you should confirm if this is the case!). 

As a side note, the schematic on this page of the github can help tease apart how to specify arguments for the sumstats function as I know it can be confusing: 
https://github.com/MichelNivard/GenomicSEM/wiki/2.-Important-resources-and-key-information

Best, 
  Andrew
